evidence: Catull. 76.13: difficile est longum subitō dēpōnere amōrem
terms.comment: “It’s difficult to …” is difficile est with an infinitive; with a verb of saying, the supine: difficile dictū est (Cic. Off. 2.48). Litotes is as common: haud facile, nōn facile.

evidence: Cic. Or. 33: magnum opus omnīnō et arduum, Brūte, cōnāmur
terms.comment: First of all “steep”: an uphill task.

phrases.latin: Nūlla est tam facilis rēs quīn difficilis siet, quam invītus faciās.
phrases.english: Nothing is so easy that it isn’t difficult when you do it against your will.

phrases.latin: Nihil tam difficile est quīn quaerendō investīgārī possiet.
phrases.english: Nothing is so difficult that it can’t be tracked down by searching.

phrases.latin: nōn quia difficilia sunt nōn audēmus, sed quia nōn audēmus difficilia sunt
phrases.english: it is not because things are difficult that we don’t dare; it is because we don’t dare that they are difficult

sources: Lewis & Short: difficilis · Lewis & Short: arduus
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 304.
